applicability: When reasoning about PyPTO source semantics in the memory domain
body:
This reference indexes the public source-level semantics for the memory domain.

- Cache Policy, Streaming Reads, and L2 Residency Warming: `pl.set_cache_policy(tensor, pl.CachePolicy.BYPASS)` declares every read of a tensor in a scope streaming; `pl.load(..., cache=...)` declares one access. BYPASS is a coherence and no-reuse contract, not a hint. The installed toolchain has no L2-bypass path yet, so it warns and compiles as an ordinary cached access.
- Cube Tile Sizing Against Mat, Acc, Vec, and the 512-Byte Line: Choose M, N, and K by ranking shapes, rejecting them against the compiler's Mat/Acc/Vec report, then measuring survivors. Growing N or K increases the L1 weight fragment; growing M or N increases the L0C accumulator; a K-contiguous transfer below the cache-line floor can lose more than a wider N gains.
- Address Allocation, DSA-RP, and Cross-Core Reserve Buffers: `AllocateMemoryAddr` gives concrete addresses to non-DDR MemRefs. PYPTO uses deterministic 32-byte-aligned sequential allocation per space; DSA_RP solves capacity-constrained placement with reuse penalties; PTOAS skips the pass. `pl.reserve_buffer` and cross-core pipe rings can dominate an overflow.
- Memory Hierarchy and Legal Data Movement: DDR, Vec, Mat, Left, Right, Acc, and Bias are separate buffers, not nested regions. A DDR-facing load can land only in Vec or Mat; specialized matmul spaces are reached by `pl.move` or written by `pl.matmul`.
- Opportunistic Memory Reuse and Author-Declared Allocations: `MemoryReuse` coalesces tiles with non-overlapping lifetimes in the same space, subject to no-alias constraints and a pipeline-stage capacity guard. Author-declared `pl.MemRef` allocations are pinned and isolated; they trade capacity for scheduling independence and have planner-specific restrictions.
- Runtime Scopes, Ring Heaps, and Intermediate Lifetime: A runtime scope is both a dependency-tracking boundary and a heap tier. Four ring sets are selected by scope nesting depth, so placing scopes changes when intermediate GM tensors are reclaimed. Memory is freed at scope exit and FIFO reclaim, not at last use.
- Scalar Access and the 64-Byte Write Granularity: `pl.read`/`pl.write` reach one element through the issuing core's data cache, and cache write-back happens in whole 64-byte lines. Concurrent task instances must own whole lines; disjoint element indices are not enough.
- Scope Stats and Ring Deadlock Diagnosis: `enable_scope_stats` records task-window, heap, dependency-pool, and tensormap usage at every scope boundary. The first JSONL line proves effective ring capacities; paired begin/end samples show high-water, live occupancy, and allocation throughput, while `orch_error_code` names the resource that wedged.
- Slicing, Valid Shapes, Padding, and Shape Views: A tile has an allocated shape and an optional valid region. Loads and slices only read source bytes that exist, reductions see the padding, and `fillpad`/`set_validshape` make the tail explicit. Argument order and view restrictions differ between `pl.slice`, `pl.load`, and `pl.store`.
title: Memory API and mechanism index
